<!-- docs-drift-check -->
### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **2** package(s): `@objectstack/metadata-protocol`, `@objectstack/runtime`, touching **3** documentable anchor(s).

**4** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/deployment/app-dependencies.mdx`  _(via installPackage (symbol, a top-level function))_
- `content/docs/kernel/contracts/metadata-service.mdx`  _(via /api/v1/packages/:packageId (route, bridged from symbol installPackage — its route source's handler names it))_
- `content/docs/permissions/system-context.mdx`  _(via handlePackagesRequest (symbol, a top-level function))_
- `content/docs/protocol/kernel/error-handling.mdx`  _(via /api/v1/packages/:packageId (route, bridged from symbol installPackage — its route source's handler names it))_

⛔ **4** release-owned page(s) also name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/v12.mdx`  _(via installPackage (symbol, a top-level function))_
- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-0.mdx`  _(via /api/v1/packages/:packageId (route, bridged from symbol installPackage — its route source's handler names it))_
- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-4.mdx`  _(via /api/v1/packages/:packageId (route, bridged from symbol installPackage — its route source's handler names it))_
- `content/docs/releases/v18/18-2.mdx`  _(via installPackage (symbol, a top-level function))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- the SDK route bridge reached **60** of **216** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **156** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **156**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **101** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **33** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 7f4cbc9d977478a161a61d4c4ba5635755934271` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `c88398d28a5c2bd8210cb89f44f6fa96db31f476` — the merge of head `8c77b8d5cb1fe0487835cab4857afd19fa4f14c6` into base `7f4cbc9d977478a161a61d4c4ba5635755934271`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin c88398d28a5c2bd8210cb89f44f6fa96db31f476 && git checkout c88398d28a5c2bd8210cb89f44f6fa96db31f476
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 7f4cbc9d977478a161a61d4c4ba5635755934271 8c77b8d5cb1fe0487835cab4857afd19fa4f14c6 && git checkout -B drift-repro 7f4cbc9d977478a161a61d4c4ba5635755934271 && git merge --no-ff 8c77b8d5cb1fe0487835cab4857afd19fa4f14c6

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 7f4cbc9d977478a161a61d4c4ba5635755934271
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 7f4cbc9d977478a161a61d4c4ba5635755934271` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

Inputs: card #28816 (body and every comment, the claim 6564922254 and the dev report 6565608722 included), PR #28842 (body, 13-file list, three-dot diff against `main`), the check-runs on the head, and the two bodies of `docs/NORTH-STAR.md` read from the API (`main` and the head). Readers of North Star titles were read with `git grep` over `origin/main` and over the head commit object; nothing was built, run or re-run.

### ① Derived judgments

- **Accept set and public surface: unchanged — right.** Every path is prose or a comment. The two source trees touched (`packages/lint`, `ui/packages/types`) change only a comment inside a test file; no export, schema, CLI flag or route moves. Nothing a metadata author can write changes.
- **The governing original moves from Chinese to English — right, and faithful.** Mechanically, over the 125-line body: 125 lines in / 125 out, every line keeps its shape (h1 / bold head / ladder row / numbered / blank), 80 ladder rows in / 80 out, and on every row the `axis`, the `checklist area` and the `item ids` are byte-identical to `main`; the road steps ① to ⑥ keep their numbers and order; the four `Priority` items keep their numbers; zero CJK characters remain. Read sentence by sentence, no rule is strengthened, weakened or dropped: the P0/P2 reading of the road, the "change the table, never re-grade card by card" rule, Priority 3's lane-queue rule, Priority 4's loud-refusal / honoured-at-runtime / designer-standard / "one wrong sentence is a product defect" rules, Stage posture's no-alias retirement, the four answers of Instruments serve the fleet, Not now and The ledger all carry over as written. The one marker 「清单项待写」 becomes `(checklist item to be written)` on the one row that carries it on `main` (L96, `standalone-boot-no-cloud`); the card's "three rows" count is stale against `main`, as the dev report says. One wording ambiguity is a should-fix under ④, not a changed rule.
- **Retiring `## English summary` — right.** No anchor `english-summary` and no link to it exists anywhere on the head; the one prose reader (`CONTRIBUTING.md` L116, "an English summary closes it") is corrected in this PR. The three surviving "English summary" hits are two release-owned CHANGELOG entries and a ui test comment about a diagnostics payload, none about this file.
- **Title readers — all renamed, spellings match the file.** On the head, `git grep` for each old title (路上的功能点, 仪器为车队服务, 现在不做, 唯一的度量, 什么算做好, 做出来的是什么, 我们是什么, 「优先级」, 〈优先级〉, 〈阶段姿态〉 as citations) returns zero hits outside the three carve-outs the card allows: revision history in `docs/qa/platform-checklist/areas/studio-authoring.json` (清单项待写), the release-owned `ui/packages/types/CHANGELOG.md` (〈阶段姿态〉), and a generic help string in `plugin-sharing` (给谁, not a reference). Every new spelling a reader uses — `Features on the road` (SKILL.md L120, AGENTS.md L206), `Priority` (execution-duties L49, filing-gate L37, triage-duties L58, lint test L48/L315, AGENTS.md L206), `What gets built` (filing-gate L25, triage-duties L59, checklist README L305, ensure-pm-labels L571), `Instruments serve the fleet` (filing-gate L49, lanes/skills L22/L23, lanes/spec L23), `Not now` (ensure-pm-labels L595), `Stage posture` (ui types test L24) — matches the bold head in `docs/NORTH-STAR.md` on the head character for character. The checklist README's quoted definition clause ("missing any one of these, it is not this application") matches L7.
- **Ratchet arithmetic — right.** No ceilinged file gains a line (SKILL.md 319, execution-duties 188, filing-gate 66, lanes/skills 32, lanes/spec 42, triage-duties 102, AGENTS.md 1050, all unchanged). The one table row touched, SKILL.md L120, is 338 bytes against the `MAX_TABLE_ROW_BYTES` pin of 341. Every edited bullet stays under the 120-byte cap: filing-gate L49 grows 113 → 119, lanes/spec L23 77 → 83, lanes/skills L22 119 → 115 and L23 115 → 115 (re-cut in place), triage-duties L58/L59 and execution-duties L49 shrink. No ceiling and no pin moved.
- **Base drift — no conflict.** `main` has moved five commits past the merge base (3cb8553c94 → 839aae58c2); none of the five touches a hits file or adds a reader of a North Star title (checked by `git grep` over `origin/main`); the API reports the PR mergeable.
- **Check-runs on the head, read at 2026-11-01T23:48Z:** success — Lint & Repo Gates and every lane inside it (Lint · PM dispatch-gates, Lint · docs & code guards, Lint · repo & tooling gates, Lint · CI, release & engine gates, Lint · ESLint, the three scoped lanes), Type Check · source gates, Type Check · debt ledger, Type Check · consumer gates, Governed Surface Queue Guard, Check Documentation Links, Check Changeset, Check PR Size, PR-body guards, Flag docs affected by code changes, Build Core, Build UI Deps, Build & E2E UI, Live E2E UI, Dogfood Regression Gate, Auto Label; no run on the head has failed. Still in progress at that reading: Test Core (8 shards), Test UI (16 shards), Type Check · workspace, Type Check UI, Lint UI. None of the in-progress families reads a hits file; the two test files whose comments changed sit in Test Core and Test UI, which the dev report shows green file-by-file locally. This record does not convert an in-progress run into a success; the Tier H approver reads them completed.

### ② Semver level

`skip-changeset` is right: no released package publishes a byte from this diff (prose, agent instruction text and comments only). `Clause-②: no` and `Metadata-protocol: none` on the PR body are right — no accept set widens or narrows, no key is added, narrowed or re-meant. Check Changeset: success.

### ③ Boundary flags

- Dev deviation 1 (`CONTRIBUTING.md`, checklist README and two test-file comments renamed although outside the card's *Measured* list): **right.** The card's own test — zero old-title hits outside revision history — reaches them; leaving them would have failed the card's test.
- Dev deviation 2 (PR-body footer shape, trailer case): a PR-body matter, not the tree; nothing to judge here.
- Dev deviation 3 (worktree left in place for this review): not used — this review was read-only, as the brief orders; the seat removes it.
- Dev deviation 4 (`pnpm --dir ui exec vitest run scripts/` first refused on an unbuilt `@objectstack/client`): not a finding; Test UI on the head is the verdict.
- `open_questions` 1 (keep the English title alone inside 「」 in the Chinese pm-dispatch files, or add a Chinese gloss): **answered — A, keep the English title alone.** `lanes/skills.md` L24 states the rule itself: 内部指令面中文,机器判据恒英文 — the prose stays Chinese and the name it points at is now English; the section has exactly one name, and a gloss would re-create the two-spelling drift the card retires and cost ratchet bytes on lines already at 115–119 B. The pm-dispatch files already quote English identifiers inside 「」 (「功能点位次」 beside `area:*`, `Path:` lines), so the form is not new.
- `open_questions` 2 (the road paragraph says four promises and lists five): **answered — A, leave as written.** The count mismatch is on `main` (L11: 四个承诺 … ① · ②③ · ④ · ⑤ · ⑥) and is content the card's *Not here* excludes; translating it as written is right. Escalated as a one-line note for the maintainer, outside this PR: the sentence counts four promises and names five steps (five items, or four if ②③ is read as one), and only the maintainer can say which.
- `out_of_scope_findings` 2 (one marker row today, not three): verified on `main` — only L96 carries 「清单项待写」; the card measured an older tree.

### ④ Design judgment

Judged against the card's eval: a reader who knows only the head's English file must follow the same rules a reader of `main`'s Chinese file follows, and every reader of a section title must still resolve.

- **`docs/NORTH-STAR.md`** — holds, with two should-fixes. Row by row and sentence by sentence the English carries the same rules (① above). The ladder is read by no script (every scripts/pm reader matches the path only: `check-governed-merges.mjs` row `north-star`, `check-governed-queue-guard.mjs`, `fleet-write/ops.mjs`, `dispatch-gates.self-test.mjs`), so the marker's new spelling after a space breaks no parser.
  - **should-fix** — L115 "p3 or not done" and L121 "if it cannot be said, it is not done" render 不做 as "not done", while L9 defines "done" as having passed verification ("What counts as done"). An English-only triage reader can take L121 as "the card cannot be marked done" (hold it) where the Chinese says "do not do it" (close it; `triage-duties.md` 无则关). A reading with one meaning: "p3 or not taken on" / "if it cannot be said, it is not taken on" (or "is not built"). The retired summary carried the same phrase, so this is inherited, but the English is now the governing text and should not need the Chinese to disambiguate.
  - **should-fix** — five live code comments quote the Chinese clause-4 sentence verbatim as what "北极星 clause 4 names in as many words": `packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-package-install.ts` L150, `packages/runtime/src/domains/packages.ts` L1500 and L1573, `packages/runtime/src/domains/packages-install-manifest-id.test.ts` L19, `packages/runtime/src/domains/packages-install-manifest-version.test.ts` L17 (「错的必须被响亮拒绝并给处方,永不静默落库」). On the head that sentence no longer exists in the file; its English (L117, "what is wrong must be loudly refused with a prescription, never silently stored") does. The clause number still resolves and the meaning is unchanged, so no rule moves — but a reader who greps the quoted words finds nothing. Outside the card's title test (a quoted sentence is not a section title), so a follow-up in the owning lanes, or this PR if the dev prefers: re-quote in the head's English, or label the Chinese as the pre-translation wording. Not a FAIL.
- **`.claude/skills/pm-dispatch/SKILL.md`** L120 — holds. 「Features on the road」 names the bold head at L13 on the head exactly; the rule (candidate order = the parent card's position on the ladder) is unchanged; 338 B against the 341 B table-row pin.

L49 at 119 B.
- **`references/lanes/skills.md`** L22, L23 — holds. The re-cut drops 本车道 (L22) and 席位 (L23); both are the file's own subject (a lane job description addressed to the seat, L1–L3), so no rule loses a home, which is the test the file's own L20 sets (被砍内容若在别处无家,砍掉就是丢规则). The rules — findings go to triage first-touch; an unanswerable Instruments question ⇒ recommend p3 or not-do, never self-enqueue — read the same. 115 B each.

- **`references/triage-duties.md`** L58, L59 — holds. 「Priority」1–3 条 resolves to head L114–116, 「What gets built」 to head L7; the `Path:` line shape is untouched.
- **`AGENTS.md`** L206 — holds. Directive 8 now names *Features on the road* and *Priority* in italics, both the bold heads on the head; the rule (a change that advances no ladder row probably should not ship) is unchanged; AGENTS.md stays 1050 lines; `check:pm-governed-prose` (Lint · PM dispatch-gates) success, the governed-surface paragraph of Directive 14 is untouched.
